PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Prenatal screening for common trisomies
Gestational Age at Sampling: [redacted] weeks
Indication: Advanced maternal age

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Test Code: QFPCR-TRI

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes extracted from amniotic fluid. This rapid molecular technique targets specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 to detect the most common autosomal trisomies.

STR Markers Analyzed:
- Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
- Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S390, D18S386
- Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S1411, D21S1412, D21S1437

DNA was extracted using QIAamp DNA Mini Kit. PCR amplification was performed using fluorescently labeled primers, and products were analyzed on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak area ratios were calculated for all informative markers.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: NORMAL COMPLEMENT
- All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns
- Peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
- No evidence of trisomy 13

Chromosome 18: NORMAL COMPLEMENT
- All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns
- Peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
- No evidence of trisomy 18

Chromosome 21: NORMAL COMPLEMENT
- All informative markers showed normal biallelic patterns
- Peak ratios within normal range (0.8-1.4)
- No evidence of trisomy 21

Fetal Sex: [redacted]
Maternal Cell Contamination: Not detected

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates a normal chromosomal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No abnormalities detected in the tested chromosomes.

LIMITATIONS
This test specifically screens for trisomies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. It does not detect:
- Structural chromosomal abnormalities
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Abnormalities of other chromosomes
- Balanced rearrangements
- Single gene disorders

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured amniocytes is recommended to follow this rapid screening test. Cell culture has been initiated and karyotype results will be reported separately in approximately 10-14 days. This will provide comprehensive cytogenetic analysis of all chromosomes.

This report has been reviewed and authorized by:
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Cytogenetics Laboratory
[redacted date]
